business_scope.primary_industry_name: Personal Wealth Analytics and Investment Tracking Cloud

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United Kingdom - Bermuda Double Taxation Arrangement (limited scope, providing UK tax credit relief for Bermuda tax and exchange of information protections)
United States - Bermuda Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (extended by the United Kingdom to Bermuda)

No substantive UK Bilateral Investment Treaty is extended to Bermuda; investor protection derives from Bermuda domestic statute and the constitutional safeguards of the British Overseas Territory framework

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Bermuda AML/CFT framework is governed by the Proceeds of Crime Act 1997 (as amended); the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2008 (as amended); the Bermuda Monetary Authority Act 1969; the Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2015 (registration, general partner and beneficial ownership identification duties); the Beneficial Ownership (Companies and Limited Liability Companies) Regulations 2017 and amendatory statutes (applied as guidance to partnership vehicles); and the Sanctions (EU Exit) (Overseas Territories) Order 2020 as extended to Bermuda. Supervision and enforcement rest with the Registrar of Companies, the Bermuda Monetary Authority, and the Financial Intelligence Agency under the Commission of Inquiry style oversight of the Bermuda Financial Intelligence Agency Act 2007.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all partners, beneficiaries, UBOs, General Partner controllers and senior managing agents against the following sources: (i) the consolidated UK Sanctions List maintained by HM Treasury under the Sanctions (EU Exit) (Overseas Territories) Order 2020 as extended to Bermuda; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists; (iii) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, given the use of USD payment rails via Stripe and Apple IAP; and (iv) the Bermuda Monetary Authority AML/ATF Guidance Notes. Politically Exposed Persons, their family members and close associates attract mandatory enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, ongoing transaction monitoring, and filing obligations to the Bermuda Financial Intelligence Agency under the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2008.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Bermuda Registrar of Companies official online name search and clearance portal operated by the Ministry of Finance (www.roc.gov.bm)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: English is the sole statutory language of Bermuda. Partnership names must be expressed in Latin (Roman) script only; no parallel transliteration or non-Roman script is permitted. An Exempted Limited Partnership name must end with 'Limited Partnership' or the approved suffix 'LP'/'L.P.' and must not be identical or misleadingly similar to any existing registered entity name in Bermuda.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Bermuda does not operate a stand-alone name reservation mechanism; name clearance is granted contemporaneously with the filing of the proposed Exempted Limited Partnership name and is deemed valid for 30 days from grant, after which re-clearance is required if the registration has not been completed. Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days, attaching a comparative table of already-registered names and legal submissions on absence of confusing similarity. Where the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may institute judicial review proceedings in the Supreme Court of Bermuda under the Rules of the Supreme Court 1985 within 21 days of the final refusal, with the Attorney-General as respondent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or mailbox-only arrangement is not acceptable. The Exempted Limited Partnerships Act 2015 requires a physical registered office in Bermuda maintained by a licensed registered agent for service of process and statutory record-keeping. For this low-risk Fintech software analytics vehicle, a substance-light structure using the registered agent's physical Bermuda address is permissible, provided the Partnership Agreement, partner register, UBO declarations and accounting records are retained at that office and the General Partner maintains a formal agency relationship with the Bermuda registered agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk of approximately 2-4% per annum for a non-licensed, low-risk software analytics and portfolio tracking entity with no Bermuda client-facing regulated activity. The probability of unannounced on-site inspection rises to 20-30% if the Registrar of Companies or the Bermuda Monetary Authority determines that AML-relevant activity, payment processing, or investment intermediation is being conducted from the Bermuda office.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Act 1883 (as amended), ss. 3, 4, 5A and 7; Exempted Partnerships Act 1969; Business Licensing Act 2011 (if domestic local trade is conducted)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Registries, Ministry of Finance, Government of Bermuda
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration as an Exempted Limited Partnership and Declaration of Limited Partnership
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital commitments are contractual and no escrow account is required by Bermuda law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that: 1. step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Proposed Name and Obtain Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Name Clearance Unit, Bermuda Registries (online via Bermuda Registries e-Services portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application with the proposed entity name, including 'LP' or 'Limited Partnership' and an 'Exempted' designation or otherwise demonstrating non-resident ownership. Pay the name search fee and provide evidence of consent if the name is similar to an existing entity.
required_dossiers: Completed Name Reservation / Name Clearance Application
Certificate of Incorporation of corporate General Partner or passport copy of individual General Partner
Proof of registered office address intimation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of confusion or undesirability, submit an alternative name for re-clearance or file a written appeal with the Registrar within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Limited Partnership Agreement and Partner Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel and Bermuda Notary Public (notaries) for signature verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Limited Partnership Agreement, clearly defining the General Partner, Limited Partners, capital commitments, profit-sharing, and scope of business as 'personal wealth analytics and investment tracking cloud software'. Have the General Partner and all Limited Partners execute the instrument; arrange notarization and, if applicable, certified English translations.
required_dossiers: Capital contribution statement or letter of commitment
Power of attorney for any represented Limited Partner
Notarised consent to act as registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the scope or partner schedule, amend the Schedule of Partners and re-execute; a full re-notarization is not required if only the schedule is updated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration of Limited Partnership and Pay Government Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Registries, Government of Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Declaration of Limited Partnership together with the name clearance certificate, registered office consent, registered agent appointment, and the prescribed government fee. Submit through the Bermuda Registries e-Services portal or in person at Hamilton; retain the stamped duplicate as proof of filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected for defective or incomplete details, file a corrective amended Declaration within 10 business days; no additional penalty is imposed if correction is made before certificate refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Limited Partnership and Post-Registration Evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Legal Instruments Desk, Bermuda Registries
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Limited Partnership with the registered number and formation date. Verify all details, then request certified copies of the certificate and a current registry extract for anti-money-laundering / know-your-client purposes at banks and payment processors.
required_dossiers: Registry extract of exempted limited partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains an error, submit a written rectification request to the Registrar under the registry correction procedure; a small rectification fee may apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Initial Governance Resolutions, Appoint Officers and Open Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Partner / Board of Directors of the General Partner; Bermuda licensed bank or eligible EMI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first partnership meeting or pass a written resolution adopting the Limited Partnership Agreement, appointing the General Partner, resident representative and compliance officer, approving the registered office, authorising Stripe and Apple IAP payment rails, and authorising opening a corporate bank account. Submit the complete KYB package to the chosen Bermuda bank or electronic money institution.
required_dossiers: AML/KYC forms for the General Partner and ultimate beneficial owners
Registered office consent and utility bill evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or EMI requests additional UBO details, provide an organisational chart and beneficial ownership declaration; supplement with revised minutes or resolutions as requested by the financial institution.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — non-manufacturing digital service; no industrial facility or local industrial licence required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No Bermuda industrial operating licence is required for cloud-based financial portfolio tracking. If a physical office is later opened in Bermuda, a Bermuda Business Licence may be required under the Business Licensing Act 2011 from the Ministry of Economy and Labour.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Bermuda Department of Environment and Natural Resources
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category 4: office and cloud software operations only; no Environmental Impact Assessment report or registration required unless a physical data centre or warehousing facility is established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable for the digital software activity; for any physical office occupancy, comply with the Bermuda Waste Management (Waste Control) Regulations and Bermuda Building Code for HVAC and electrical equipment; no VOCs or industrial discharges expected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Bermuda Fire and Rescue Service is required for any occupied commercial premises in Bermuda; structural load certification and safe-occupancy clearance apply to a physical office. Telework and cloud-only operators require no civil-defence or occupational clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda (entity registration and economic substance filings); Office of the Tax Commissioner (payroll tax administration); Bermuda Customs Department (customs duties). Primary portal: www.gov.bm
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Bermuda imposes no corporate or income tax; thus no general income tax TIN is issued. A foreign-owned Exempted Limited Partnership (ELP) must register under the Exempted Partnerships Act 2015 with the Registrar of Companies, filing a declaration of partnership and paying applicable fees. Upon registration, the entity receives a Government Registration Number (GRN), which serves as its primary identification for all government agencies. If the ELP has employees in Bermuda, it must register separately with the Office of the Tax Commissioner for payroll tax and obtain a payroll tax reference number. No VAT/GST registration is possible or required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Bermuda does not offer domestic 'check-the-box' or hybrid mismatch elections because direct taxation is absent. Under foreign tax systems, the ELP may be treated as fiscally transparent (default) or may elect corporate classification if the applicable foreign tax code (e.g., US USCT §7701) permits. In Bermuda, the Economic Substance Regulations impose substance requirements on relevant activities but do not provide any tax classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT or GST; Bermuda levies customs duties and stamp duties under the Customs Tariff Act 1968.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable; Bermuda has no VAT/GST registration threshold. Any business importing goods into Bermuda must hold a valid customs importer registration and could be subject to customs duties based on the value of goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API e-invoicing, or digital stamping regime exists. Customs declarations are submitted electronically via the Bermuda Customs Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) portal for import/export documentation purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable. Bermuda does not impose VAT/GST on any supplies, and therefore there is no export zero-rating mechanism. Goods exported from Bermuda are not subject to customs duties upon export, and certain goods imported for subsequent re-export may qualify for duty relief under the Temporary Importation / Bonded Warehouse schemes.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (if goods are controlled or exceed threshold)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Bermuda Customs Export Permit (for controlled/restricted goods)
Certificate of Origin (if required by destination country)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: No VAT/GST clawback provisions exist in Bermuda. However, fraudulent customs declarations, including misrepresentation of export eligibility or duty relief, are penalised under the Customs Tariff Act 1968: fines up to BMD 5,000, imprisonment up to two years, forfeiture of goods, and potential suspension of customs broker or importer licensing. Retrospective clawbacks are limited to recovery of unpaid customs duties plus penalties; no direct tax clawbacks apply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bermuda Monetary Authority (BMA) — the integrated financial services regulator and monetary authority for the Bermuda jurisdiction; the Bank of England retains nominal monetary oversight over UK Overseas Territories for systemic risk coordination.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Bermuda operates a fully convertible currency regime for both current and capital account transactions. The Bermuda Dollar (BMD) is pegged 1:1 to the US Dollar (USD) and is issued by the BMA within Bermuda. There are no exchange control restrictions under the Bermuda Exchange Control Act 1972, as modified by the BMA's delegation of authority to recognised banks for routine transactions. Profit remittances, capital repatriation, and income distributions from an Exempted Limited Partnership are freely permitted without hard currency approval. Dividends, liquidation proceeds, and partnership allocations can be converted and transferred offshore without any hurdle. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, are unrestricted for non-resident partners. The only formality is standard suspicious transaction reporting under the Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing regime. Therefore, the jurisdiction provides a zero-friction convertibility and remittance environment for the target ISIC 6201 software platform.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Bermuda imposes no statutory timeline for export proceeds surrender and has no mandatory conversion ratio for foreign currency receipts. The Exchange Control Act 1972 was substantially liberalised; authorised banks handle all routine inward and outward wires. For the fintech software revenue streams flowing via Stripe and Apple IAP into a Bermuda operational account, the USD-equivalent balance is freely retained, held in BMD or USD, and deployed for trade disbursements without any mandatory central bank surrender. There is no obligation to convert export receipts into local currency. The only compliance requirement is maintaining proper bookkeeping records under the Partnership Act 2006 and the BMA's AML/ATF guidance to substantiate the source of funds for the underlying digital service exports.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low — Medium. Offshore digital electronic money institutions (EMIs) domiciled in the UK or EU (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise, Paysera) do not possess a Bermuda Money Service Business (MSB) license and therefore cannot be used as a primary bank account for the Bermuda ELP in a manner that satisfies BMA substance expectations. A UK-authorised EMI may offer a multi-currency IBAN for operational convenience, but settlement into Bermuda's regulated banking system still requires a tier-1 local bank account. The ELP may use an EMI as an auxiliary collection rail for Stripe payouts, but only if the EMI is fully KYC-compliant and the ELP maintains transparent flow-through records to the BMA-regulated bank. Legal constraints include: (1) EMIs are not supervised under the Bermuda Banking Act 1969; (2) foreign EMI accounts do not provide a Bermuda clearing footprint or local BMA reporting; (3) corporate treasury risk is higher because EMIs are not covered by Bermuda deposit insurance. Recommended structure: use a regulated bank as the principal account and an EMI only as a low-velocity receiving intermediate with automatic sweep to the bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Bermuda's AML/ATF regime requires the ultimate beneficial owners and general partner representatives to undergo identity verification. Banks generally mandate at least one authorised signatory or partner to appear physically in Bermuda for the initial relationship onboarding if the ELP has non-resident owners. Remote opening is possible on a case-by-case basis through video interviews, notarised passport copies, and apostilled partnership documents, but the BMA's practical expectation for an exempted partnership with US/UK principals is an in-person or video interview conducted by the relationship manager. A direct physical presence is not a statutory codified requirement under the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2018 for remote clients, yet many banks apply a 'first account opening' face-to-face policy. To avoid delays, the ELP should appoint a Bermuda-resident local contact or corporate service provider as a liaison. A video-KYC with live identity evidence upload is usually acceptable if the partnership has no negative media, a clear source of wealth, and a reputable registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exempted Limited Partnership with a foreign general partner and opaque multi-tier ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified ELP Certificate of Formation, executed limited partnership agreement, legal opinion from Bermuda counsel, full ownership chain to ultimate beneficial owners, proof of principal's physical residential address, bank references from the parent group, and an organisational chart showing the UK digital trading entity as the general partner with clear partner capital commitments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds derived from cross-border fintech subscriptions, card aggregators, and app stores without a local statutory payment licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or management-prepared financial statements, platform merchant statements from Stripe/Apple, revenue waterfall model clearly showing SaaS subscription flows, demonstration that the activities are software/portfolio tracking rather than payment services, an independent accountant's letter confirming the absence of covered regulated activity, and transactional history showing a legitimate business pattern.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP exposure due to a US or UK-based KYC principal using third-party payment rails.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: World-Check or equivalent negative media and sanctions screening results for all natural persons and entity layers, PEP status declarations, passport and proof-of-address notarisation, CI/MOI certificate of good standing for the foreign parent, and an irrevocable undertaking to provide granular source-of-wealth documentation for any capital injections exceeding the bank's threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction nexus arising from the 'KY' jurisdiction tag in the ELP name or from non-resident ownership without Bermuda substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bermuda registered agent lease agreement, Bermuda Economic Substance Certification (if applicable), board minutes designating Bermuda office as the place of administration, annual tax filing certificates from the BMA, and a compliance pack demonstrating that the ELP's substantive management sits in an acceptable jurisdiction (UK/Bermuda) with no harmful nexus to Cayman Islands unless substantively justified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Structured bank-account misuse risk due to international cash sweeps and app-store receivables with no predictable settlement file.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A treasury policy memorandum detailing the purpose of each account, anti-money laundering escalation procedures, transaction monitoring systems, the use of 'sweep to operational account' instructions, and an automated reconciliation report separating partner capital from subscription operating cash flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from foreign partners into the Bermuda ELP must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or via bank-to-bank book transfers from a recognised correspondent bank. The compliant wire protocol is as follows: (1) sender's bank must include the beneficiary ELP name exactly as on the BMA banking records, account number, and the 'BENEFICIARY' legal entity identifier (LEI) if available; (2) the payment purpose (remittance information) field must cite 'Investment contribution to Bermuda exempted limited partnership' with an ISO 2022 structured reference; (3) the originating bank must have an AML-compliant passport of the transfer confirmation, while the receiving Bermuda bank will copy a BMA-compliant inward remittance report; (4) the eligible purpose code under the BMA's balance-of-payments classification is 'Direct Investment — Capital Contribution' (category 'F' for financial account), and the bank may request a capital account allocation schedule; (5) the funding must not be sourced from a non-bank money service business unless a full customer due diligence pack is provided to the receiving bank prior to sending. The capital should be layered through a reputable UK or US correspondent bank to avoid being flagged as 'high-risk offshore routing'. Ideal routing is: Parent operating bank (UK/US) -> Correspondent bank (e.g. Citi or HSBC) -> Bermuda Tier-1 bank -> ELP Capital Escrow Account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements from the ELP's operational account to vendors, technology suppliers, and SaaS infrastructure providers should be executed via standard SWIFT MT103 single-credit transfers for low-value non-documentary payments, or via a commercial letter of credit (documentary LC) for high-value software licensing or cloud procurement if the supplier requires guarantee-based settlement. The MT103 field 50 (ordering customer) must show the ELP as the outside party, field 59 (beneficiary) must exactly match the vendor's bank records, and field 70 (remittance information) must be explicit about 'settlement for cloud infrastructure subscription', 'royalty for software intellectual property', or 'partner distribution payable'. Commercial LCs should include an undertaking by the Bermuda bank that the presentation of a pro-forma invoice, delivery certificate, and digital acceptance is valid for the pay-out. Since Bermuda is not a commodity trade hub, the ELP should utilise a master treasury account with US dollar clearing via the New York CHIPS/Fedwire endpoint or UK CHAPS (Sterling) only if the BMD/USD conversion is required. For vendor payments in GBP or EUR, the bank will automatically clear through the standard aCH/SEPA SWIFT lanes; no special restrictions apply.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable foreign exchange forwards (BMD/USD, GBP/USD, EUR/USD) executed with a Bermuda-regulated bank, subject to BMA commercial FX guidelines.

Cross-currency swaps for medium-term treasury management when the ELP holds USD-denominated partner capital and pays GBP-denominated software licensing costs; permissible under the BMA's derivatives eligibility if the counterparty is a licensed bank or a qualifying ISDA-authorized dealer.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on currencies without local convertibility, such as RMB or INR-linked receivables, may be used only through an offshore banking counterparty with no Bermuda-licensed execution requirement; however, for BMD/USD, the peg renders NDFs redundant.
Currency options embedded in partnership money-market products are permitted but not recommended as the primary hedge due to non-profit cost burden.

Foreign exchange spot contracts are always permissible for immediate settlement of operating expenses and merchant payouts; they do not require a capital markets licence if executed as a banking transaction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Exempted Partnership Annual Return (confirming general partner, registered office, limited partner count and registered particulars)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: on or before the 60th calendar day after the anniversary of the date of registration of the ELP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fees accrue per the Registrar's published scale (first month or part: BMD 300; each additional month or part: BMD 100); unpaid annual fees accrue statutory interest; continued default triggers administrative strike-off notice in the Bermuda Gazette and automatic dissolution of the ELP's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Return or NIL Economic Substance Declaration (ES Form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Tax Commissioner of Bermuda, submitted through the Registrar of Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the ELP's financial accounting period; a calendar-period ELP is due by 1 March of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial statutory penalty of BMD 10,000 under the Economic Substance Act 2018 (as amended) for failure to file, plus escalating daily default penalties; chronic default exposes the general partner to fines, imprisonment terms, administrative strike-off, and referral to the Bermuda Monetary Authority.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed on an exempted limited partnership under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992. A compulsory independent audit arises only where: (i) the ELP is licensed or regulated by the Bermuda Monetary Authority as an investment fund, fund administrator, or financial business; (ii) the partnership agreement or investor side letters mandate audited financial statements; or (iii) group consolidation or home-jurisdiction rules of a limited partner require audited accounts. None is triggered for the present unregulated fintech SaaS portfolio-tracking structure.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Bermuda GAAP (IFRS-aligned) governs statutory financial record-keeping; regulated entities may apply IFRS or US GAAP with Bermuda Monetary Authority acceptance; financial statements are prepared on a going-concern and capital-maintenance basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Bermuda operates no public central beneficial-ownership registry. Under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1997 and Bermuda AML/ATF regulations, the ELP must maintain an accurate register of limited partners showing the ultimate beneficial owner of every transferable partnership interest. Annual confirmation is executed through the resident corporate-services provider's CDD refresh cycle; any transfer of partnership interests must be recorded in the statutory register promptly, and the annual return reflects updated ownership as at the registration anniversary.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book and resolutions of the general partner
Exempted partnership agreement and registered-office record file

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,500–US$3,500 per annum (typical Bermuda registered-office and resident corporate-services provider fee range for a single exempted limited partnership)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$6,000–US$15,000 per annum (representative certified-audit quote range for a small unregulated exempted limited partnership; not statutorily required in the base case)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (Bermuda imposes no corporate income tax; Bermuda is a non-resident offshore jurisdiction for UK tax purposes, and the UK's 25% corporation tax rate does not apply to Bermuda-incorporated entities without UK tax residence or a UK permanent establishment)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory Bermuda tax holidays; entities may rely on a Certificate of Exemption under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992 confirming tax exemption until 2035; no payroll tax or land tax applies to exempted limited partnerships without Bermuda-source income or employees; UK CTA 2009 foreign permanent establishment exemption may apply for UK-resident partners; NI contributions are not applicable absent UK presence

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Bermuda: No corporate income tax return form for ELPs; the primary filing is the Annual Certificate of Compliance (Form ARC) filed through the Bermuda Registrar of Companies' electronic portal (registry.gov.bm) or the Ministry of Finance's online system for Economic Substance Act returns
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Certificate of Compliance: due no later than 31 January following the calendar year end (31 December); Economic Substance Act annual filing: due within six months of the ELP's financial year end; UK self-assessment and partnership returns may be due 31 January after the UK tax year, but only if UK-resident partners or permanent establishment exists

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Exempted Limited Partnership exactly as registered in Bermuda
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert ELP legal name; no UK-specific NINO or UTR is required for a pure Bermuda-incorporated non-UK entity

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form ARC - Certificate of Exemption Reference
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The reference number and issue date of the tax exemption certificate issued under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the certificate number; this evidences the statutory exemption from Bermuda income tax until 2035

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical registered office address in Bermuda maintained by a licensed Bermuda service provider
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Bermuda registered agent address; do not insert a UK registered office address unless a UK PE exists

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISIC v4 code and short narrative of the ELP's principal activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ISIC 6201 (Computer programming activities) and describe the cloud portfolio tracking software application; confirm no Bermuda physical operations

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and residential or registered addresses of all general and limited partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List each non-resident partner; no Bermuda tax identification number is assigned to non-residents

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form ARC - Declaration of Exempt Status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the ELP is not carrying on business in Bermuda with the general public and has no Bermuda-source revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tick 'Exempted' status and confirm that all revenue is derived from non-Bermuda sources via cloud subscription and app stores

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: UK tax filing only required if the ELP is UK-resident or carries on a trade in the UK through a permanent establishment
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no UK tax presence, file nothing in the UK; if a UK tax presence exists, complete the SA800 partnership return allocating profits to non-resident partners in accordance with CTA 2009 and TCGA 1992

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual economic substance declaration under the Economic Substance Act 2018, applicable to relevant entities carrying on relevant activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a holding entity or finance business, confirm whether the ELP carries on relevant activity; a pure equity investment holding entity may qualify as a non-resident entity and file a NIL return if managed and controlled outside Bermuda and tax resident in a jurisdiction with a 26+% headline tax rate

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late Annual Certificate of Compliance: initial penalty of $250 rising to $500 for continued default; the Registrar may strike off the ELP for non-compliance and the Bermuda courts may impose additional restitution orders. Economic Substance Act late filing: penalty of $10,000 plus $1,000 per month of default; false filings carry penalties of up to $100,000 and imprisonment of up to five years for directors, officers, or partners. UK late partnership return penalties range from £100 to £3,000 plus daily penalties of £60 per day up to £3,000 for continued non-compliance, plus 7% interest, only where UK filing obligations arise

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Bermuda imposes no withholding tax on dividends, profits, or distributions to partners; UK dividend withholding tax to non-residents does not arise absent a UK-resident payer; the ELP converts profits to taxable income at the partner level depending on the partner's jurisdiction of residence)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because Bermuda has no UK double tax treaty and is not a party to a comprehensive UK DTA, no UK-Bermuda treaty relief protocol exists; however, the UK-Bermuda Tax Information Exchange Agreement (TIEA) provides administrative exchange of information only and does not grant withholding tax relief. If a partner is a UK tax resident, the partner must claim foreign tax credit relief unilaterally under UK Law (TIOPA 2010 ss. 8-17) by filing a UK self-assessment return and submitting the foreign tax credit claim form (s. 18 TIOPA certificate or FTCR form); for jurisdictions with a DTA with Bermuda, such as the United States or Netherlands, the limited partner must obtain a Bermuda Certificate of Tax Residence from the Bermuda Registrar and submit the relevant claim form (IRS Form 8833 or Dutch tax return) to invoke treaty benefits
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Bermuda statutory withholding tax on royalty and interest payments: 0%. UK statutory withholding tax on payments from a UK-resident payer: interest sourced in the UK is subject to 20% deduction at source under ITA 2007 s. 874 unless the UK DTA or the EU Interest and Royalties Directive is invoked, and UK-origin royalties paid to non-residents may be subject to 20% withholding under UK tax law; however, Bermuda-incorporated ELPs are not UK residents and no UK withholding applies on payments from the ELP to non-resident partners. Treaty rates do not apply on Bermuda-sourced payments because Bermuda does not impose withholding tax

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No Bermuda transfer pricing legislation; however the UK transfer pricing rules under TIOPA 2010 Part 4 apply to a Bermudian ELP if it is UK-resident, or if it has a UK PE, or if UK-resident partners hold a 25%+ participation; UK Local File and Master File documentation obligations are triggered where the UK group turnover exceeds £200 million and the ELP's cross-border related party transactions exceed £20 million; Bermuda Economic Substance Act requires documentation in the form of a written economic substance assessment and board minutes evidencing management and control in Bermuda
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) under Bermuda's Economic Substance Act 2018 apply to ELPs that carry on a relevant activity: banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, finance and leasing, headquarters, holding entity, IP, distribution and service company. The ELP in scope for ISIC 6201 provision of a cloud software application to non-residents may be classified as a 'pure equity holding entity' if it only holds the IP and equity; otherwise it must satisfy the core income-generating activities tests in Bermuda: (1) guide and manage the business in Bermuda with board meetings; (2) maintain an adequate physical presence; (3) have adequate full-time employees in Bermuda; (4) incur adequate operating expenditure in Bermuda. A reduced substance requirement applies to a pure equity holding entity, requiring only compliance with Companies Act statutory filing and adequate employment and physical presence; for tax-residency-based exemption, the ELP must be tax resident in a qualifying jurisdiction with a corporate tax rate of at least 26% (e.g. UK 25% is not sufficient; a US C-corporation partner or Singapore-resident entity may qualify if the jurisdiction applies a tax rate above 26% on the relevant income)

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False Economic Substance Declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing an Economic Substance Act return falsely declaring that the ELP is a pure equity holding entity or that it is tax resident in a qualifying jurisdiction when in fact the directors or partners exercise management and control in Bermuda and no substance exists; or failing to declare the ELP's relevant activity to avoid ESR obligations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of up to $100,000 for a false declaration or failure to file; additional penalties of $10,000 plus $1,000 per month for continued default; the Bermuda Registrar may publish the non-compliant entity's name and may place a restriction on the ELP's bank accounts and share transfers; under UK criminal provisions, cross-border tax evasion facilitation under Finance Act 2002 s. 144 is punishable by up to 7 years' imprisonment for the facilitators and unlimited fines
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Partners and managers who knowingly make false ESR declarations face civil restitution orders, personal fines, and disqualification from managing Bermuda companies; serious economic substance evasion and criminal conduct in the UK (FCA 2002 s. 144) may lead to imprisonment of directors and partners and confiscation orders equivalent to the defrauded tax plus interest and penalties

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Commercial Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Bermudian ELP as a pure shell with no physical office, no bank account, no employees in Bermuda, and no evidence of decision-making, while claiming exemption under the Certificate of Exemption and passing all profits through to non-resident principals; failure to file Annual Returns and ARC within the statutory period
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Exempted Partnerships Act 1992, a non-compliant ELP may be struck off the register and its assets vested in the Crown; under the Economic Substance Act 2018, the Registrar may impose a fine of up to $100,000 and a member of the ELP may face disgorgement of profits earned during the non-compliance period; UK anti-shell measures through the Register of Overseas Entities (UK) require the ELP to disclose beneficial owners before acquiring UK land and a failure to report can cause freezing of interests
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and limited partners who participate in management may be personally liable for the ELP's obligations if the partnership is used to defraud creditors or tax authorities; the Bermuda court may lift the limited liability veil, require civil restitution of diverted profits, and issue travel bans preventing partners from leaving Bermuda pending investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Beneficial Ownership Transparency Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the Beneficial Ownership (BO) return under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Act 2023; allowing nominee partners to conceal the ultimate beneficial owner; processing subscription revenue from a UK app store without proper AML risk assessment and knowing the source of partner funds
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML Penalties in Bermuda under the Proceeds of Crime Act 1997 and the Beneficial Ownership Act 2023: fines of up to $25,000 for failing to maintain a BO register; imprisonment of up to 5 years for wilful concealment of a beneficial owner; the ELP's bank accounts may be frozen, and the Registrar may impose a restriction notice preventing any transaction without regulator approval; UK Economic Crime Levy and the UK register of overseas entities penalties of up to £2,500 per day for non-compliance if the ELP owns UK land or enters the UK property market
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners, compliance officers, and any manager who knowingly permits untraceable partner structures or facilitates money laundering through the ELP account face personal criminal liability: up to 14 years' imprisonment under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 (UK) and up to 5 years under Bermuda law, asset forfeiture and confiscation of the full value of the software subscription revenue traceable to criminal proceeds, civil liability of directors for fines, and travel bans as a precautionary measure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Cross-Border Permanent Establishment and UK Attribution Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the cloud-based portfolio tracking business such that UK-resident staff or a UK Stripe merchant account creates a UK permanent establishment; failing to register the ELP with HMRC for corporation tax; failing to file a UK partnership return for profits deemed attributable to the UK PE; incorrectly claiming no UK tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: HMRC may issue discovery assessments under TMA 1970 s. 29 for tax underpaid, potentially reaching back 20 years in deliberate non-compliance cases; penalties under Schedule 24 FA 2007 may be up to 100% of the avoided tax (up to 200% for deliberately concealed cross-border arrangements); UK corporation tax at 25% may be levied on the PE-attributable profits; interest at Bank of England base rate plus 2.5% accrues daily
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners who control a UK PAYE/NIC and corporation tax evasion may be pursued personally if the ELP is an offshore façade and HMRC obtains a direction under CTA 2010 s. 797; personal liability of up to the unpaid tax, plus penalties and interest; a director may be subject to a travel restriction order, bankruptcy proceedings for tax debts, and imprisonment for up to 7 years for fraudulent evasion of income tax (TMA s. 106A)
